newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures settle up but sharply off highs.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures settle up but sharply off highs.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed firmer but sharply off the highs with the speculators cited as steady buyers and sellers, floor sources said.
Fund buying on the open lifted the benchmark July contract to the day's high of 79.80 cents, where analysts had pegged firm resistance.
Local buying kept the market steady before the speculators began to erode gains.
The front month dipped below unchanged but climbed higher on the close to settle at 77.05 cents per lb, up 0.45, having ranged from 79.80 to 76.50 cents.
Second-position September closed unchanged at 79.10 cents, while the rest of the board finished 0.75 higher to 0.50 lower.
The failure to sustain gains confirms the market's weak technical tone, analysts said, noting that open interest has continued to climb amid sharp losses.
Open interest in July rose 513 lots to 16,501 lots, as of early Friday.

The fundamental picture is also bearish. On Friday, FCOJ movement into trade channels for the week ended May 24 was pegged at 6,146,663 gallons compared with 4,911,368 gallons last week. But imports reached 768,758 gallons compared with 174,248 gallons the previous week.
There has been no change in the outlook for rising global supplies, analysts said.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its next estimate of the Florida crop on June 12. The most recent forecast put the crop at a record 224.2 million 90-lb boxes, and yields at 1.58 gallons per box.
Technical support remained at the recent low of 74.90 cents, followed by 74.30 and then 72.00 cents.
An estimated 3,200 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Friday's official 3,070 lots.
